sanskrit: ā no̍ de̱vānā̱m upa̍ vetu̱ śaṁso̱ viśve̍bhis tu̱rair ava̍se̱ yaja̍traḥ | tebhi̍r va̱yaṁ su̍ṣa̱khāyo̍ bhavema̱ tara̍nto̱ viśvā̍ duri̱tā syā̍ma ||
english: May the praise of the gods, the adorable one with all swift helpers, come to us for our protection. Through them may we become good companions, crossing over all adversities.

sanskrit: pari̍ ci̱n marto̱ dravi̍ṇam mamanyād ṛ̱tasya̍ pa̱thā nama̱sā vi̍vāset | u̱ta svena̱ kratu̍nā̱ saṁ va̍deta̱ śreyā̍ṁsa̱ṁ dakṣa̱m mana̍sā jagṛbhyāt ||
english: A mortal may well desire wealth; let him move along the path of Ṛta with reverence. Let him also speak in accord with his own understanding; with his mind let him grasp the superior discernment.

sanskrit: adhā̍yi dhī̱tir asa̍sṛgra̱m aṁśā̍s tī̱rthe na da̱smam upa̍ ya̱nty ūmā̍ḥ | a̱bhy ā̍naśma suvi̱tasya̍ śū̱ṣaṁ nave̍daso a̱mṛtā̍nām abhūma ||
english: The prayer has been set in place; the portions have been released; the waves approach the wondrous one as at a sacred ford. We have attained the vigour of blessedness; we have become those who know the immortals.

sanskrit: nitya̍ś cākanyā̱t svapa̍ti̱r damū̍nā̱ yasmā̍ u de̱vaḥ sa̍vi̱tā ja̱jāna̍ | bhago̍ vā̱ gobhi̍r arya̱mem a̍najyā̱t so a̍smai̱ cāru̍ś chadayad u̱ta syā̍t ||
english: The house-lord who is perpetually brilliant, the home-companion for whom the god Savitṛ has given birth — may Bhaga anoint his face with cattle, may he be pleasing and auspicious to him.

sanskrit: i̱yaṁ sā bhū̍yā u̱ṣasā̍m iva̱ kṣā yad dha̍ kṣu̱manta̱ḥ śava̍sā sa̱māya̍n | a̱sya stu̱tiṁ ja̍ri̱tur bhikṣa̍māṇā̱ ā na̍ḥ śa̱gmāsa̱ upa̍ yantu̱ vājā̍ḥ ||
english: May this earth be as it is at dawns, when the mighty ones come together with strength. Seeking this praise of the singer, may the strengthening prizes come to us full of blessing.

sanskrit: a̱syed e̱ṣā su̍ma̱tiḥ pa̍prathā̱nābha̍vat pū̱rvyā bhūma̍nā̱ gauḥ | a̱sya sanī̍ḻā̱ asu̍rasya̱ yonau̍ samā̱na ā bhara̍ṇe̱ bibhra̍māṇāḥ ||
english: Of him has this benevolence spread wide; the ancient cow became multitudinous. His companions, in the womb of the mighty lord, are borne along equally in the same vessel.

sanskrit: kiṁ svi̱d vana̱ṁ ka u̱ sa vṛ̱kṣa ā̍sa̱ yato̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī ni̍ṣṭata̱kṣuḥ | sa̱ṁta̱sthā̱ne a̱jare̍ i̱taū̍tī̱ ahā̍ni pū̱rvīr u̱ṣaso̍ jaranta ||
english: What was the wood, what indeed was the tree from which they fashioned Heaven and Earth? The two, ageless in their standing-place, with their helpers here, have aged through the many former dawns.

sanskrit: naitāva̍d e̱nā pa̱ro a̱nyad a̍sty u̱kṣā sa dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī bi̍bharti | tvaca̍m pa̱vitra̍ṁ kṛṇuta sva̱dhāvā̱n yad ī̱ṁ sūrya̱ṁ na ha̱rito̱ vaha̍nti ||
english: There is nothing greater than this, nothing else beyond it; the strong bull bears Heaven and Earth. He who has self-power makes the pure skin, when the bay horses carry the Sun.

sanskrit: ste̱go na kṣām aty e̍ti pṛ̱thvīm miha̱ṁ na vāto̱ vi ha̍ vāti̱ bhūma̍ | mi̱tro yatra̱ varu̍ṇo a̱jyamā̍no̱ 'gnir vane̱ na vy asṛ̍ṣṭa̱ śoka̍m ||
english: Like a roof he passes over the wide earth; like mist the wind blows apart the multitude. There where Mitra and Varuṇa, the instigator, like Agni in the forest, have released their flame.

sanskrit: sta̱rīr yat sūta̍ sa̱dyo a̱jyamā̍nā̱ vyathi̍r avya̱thīḥ kṛ̍ṇuta̱ svago̍pā | pu̱tro yat pūrva̍ḥ pi̱tror jani̍ṣṭa śa̱myāṁ gaur ja̍gāra̱ yad dha̍ pṛ̱cchān ||
english: When the barren one suddenly gave birth, being impelled, making the trembling into steadiness, self-guarding — when the son was born before his parents, the cow devoured the pestle when she was asked about it.

sanskrit: u̱ta kaṇva̍ṁ nṛ̱ṣada̍ḥ pu̱tram ā̍hur u̱ta śyā̱vo dhana̱m āda̍tta vā̱jī | pra kṛ̱ṣṇāya̱ ruśa̍d apinva̱todha̍r ṛ̱tam atra̱ naki̍r asmā apīpet ||
english: They also call Kaṇva the son of Nṛṣad, and the dark horse Śyāva took the wealth. The bright one swelled out the udder for Kṛṣṇa; here none has pressed upon Ṛta for him.

sanskrit: pra su gmantā̍ dhiyasā̱nasya̍ sa̱kṣaṇi̍ va̱rebhi̍r va̱rām̐ a̱bhi ṣu pra̱sīda̍taḥ | a̱smāka̱m indra̍ u̱bhaya̍ṁ jujoṣati̱ yat so̱myasyāndha̍so̱ bubo̍dhati ||
english: Come forth, O seekers of the prayer-holder, choosing excellent things; sit down favourably upon the choicest things. Indra delights in both of ours — what he awakens of the Soma juice.

sanskrit: vī̍ndra yāsi di̱vyāni̍ roca̱nā vi pārthi̍vāni̱ raja̍sā puruṣṭuta | ye tvā̱ vaha̍nti̱ muhu̍r adhva̱rām̐ upa̱ te su va̍nvantu vagva̱nām̐ a̍rā̱dhasa̍ḥ ||
english: O Indra, praised by many, you traverse the celestial luminous realms and the earthly ones with the dust. Those who carry you repeatedly to the sacrifices — let the eloquent ones who fall short win you over.

sanskrit: tad in me̍ chantsa̱d vapu̍ṣo̱ vapu̍ṣṭaram pu̱tro yaj jāna̍m pi̱tror a̱dhīya̍ti | jā̱yā pati̍ṁ vahati va̱gnunā̍ su̱mat pu̱ṁsa id bha̱dro va̍ha̱tuḥ pari̍ṣkṛtaḥ ||
english: That which is more beautiful than the beautiful form delights me — when the son takes on the knowledge of his parents. The wife who carries her husband with voice full of goodness: the auspicious wedding adorned with a male child.

sanskrit: tad it sa̱dhastha̍m a̱bhi cāru̍ dīdhaya̱ gāvo̱ yac chāsa̍n vaha̱tuṁ na dhe̱nava̍ḥ | mā̱tā yan mantu̍r yū̱thasya̍ pū̱rvyābhi vā̱ṇasya̍ sa̱ptadhā̍tu̱r ij jana̍ḥ ||
english: That dwelling-place shines beautifully — when the cows like milk-cows point toward the wedding. When the mother of the counsellor anciently shines for the herd, the people of the seven-fold song indeed.

sanskrit: pra vo 'cchā̍ ririce deva̱yuṣ pa̱dam eko̍ ru̱drebhi̍r yāti tu̱rvaṇi̍ḥ | ja̱rā vā̱ yeṣv a̱mṛte̍ṣu dā̱vane̱ pari̍ va̱ ūme̍bhyaḥ siñcatā̱ madhu̍ ||
english: The step of the god-loving one has spread forth surpassing; the mighty one travels alone with the Rudras. For the givers among those immortals, or for old age, pour honey around for the helpers.

sanskrit: ni̱dhī̱yamā̍na̱m apa̍gūḻham a̱psu pra me̍ de̱vānā̍ṁ vrata̱pā u̍vāca | indro̍ vi̱dvām̐ anu̱ hi tvā̍ ca̱cakṣa̱ tenā̱ham a̍gne̱ anu̍śiṣṭa̱ āgā̍m ||
english: The guardian of the vows of the gods declared to me the one that is placed and hidden in the waters. Indra, being wise, has indeed beheld you; instructed by him, O Agni, I have come.

sanskrit: akṣe̍travit kṣetra̱vida̱ṁ hy aprā̱ṭ sa praiti̍ kṣetra̱vidānu̍śiṣṭaḥ | e̱tad vai bha̱dram a̍nu̱śāsa̍nasyo̱ta sru̱tiṁ vi̍ndaty añja̱sīnā̍m ||
english: The one who knows not the field questioned the one who knows the field; he proceeds, instructed by the field-knower. This indeed is the auspiciousness of instruction — and he finds the stream of the straight paths.

sanskrit: a̱dyed u̱ prāṇī̱d ama̍mann i̱māhāpī̍vṛto adhayan mā̱tur ūdha̍ḥ | em e̍nam āpa jari̱mā yuvā̍na̱m ahe̍ḻa̱n vasu̍ḥ su̱manā̍ babhūva ||
english: Today it has breathed without thinking; covered by these days, it drank from the mother's udder. Old age came upon this youthful one; unangered, the good one became of pleasant disposition.

sanskrit: e̱tāni̍ bha̱drā ka̍laśa kriyāma̱ kuru̍śravaṇa̱ dada̍to ma̱ghāni̍ | dā̱na id vo̍ maghavāna̱ḥ so a̍stv a̱yaṁ ca̱ somo̍ hṛ̱di yam bibha̍rmi ||
english: Let us do these auspicious things, O vessel; O Kuruśravaṇa, the gift of bounties. Let giving indeed be yours, O Generous One; and may this Soma which I bear in my heart be yours.

sanskrit: pra mā̍ yuyujre pra̱yujo̱ janā̍nā̱ṁ vahā̍mi sma pū̱ṣaṇa̱m anta̍reṇa | viśve̍ de̱vāso̱ adha̱ mām a̍rakṣan du̱ḥśāsu̱r āgā̱d iti̱ ghoṣa̍ āsīt ||
english: The inciters of the people have yoked me; I carry Pūṣan between them. Then all the gods protected me; the cry arose: 'One who commands ill has come.'

sanskrit: sam mā̍ tapanty a̱bhita̍ḥ sa̱patnī̍r iva̱ parśa̍vaḥ | ni bā̍dhate̱ ama̍tir na̱gnatā̱ jasu̱r ver na ve̍vīyate ma̱tiḥ ||
english: The ribs scorch me on all sides like rival wives. Poverty, nakedness presses me down; thought flutters about like a bird weary of its course.

sanskrit: mūṣo̱ na śi̱śnā vy a̍danti mā̱dhya̍ḥ sto̱tāra̍ṁ te śatakrato | sa̱kṛt su no̍ maghavann indra mṛḻa̱yādhā̍ pi̱teva̍ no bhava ||
english: The middlemen eat up the praises like mice their phalluses, O Śatakratu. Just once, O bountiful Indra, be merciful to us; thereafter be like a father to us.

sanskrit: ku̱ru̱śrava̍ṇam āvṛṇi̱ rājā̍na̱ṁ trāsa̍dasyavam | maṁhi̍ṣṭhaṁ vā̱ghatā̱m ṛṣi̍ḥ ||
english: I choose Kuruśravaṇa, the king, the descendant of Trasadasyu — most bounteous of those who are priests of the sacred song, the seer.

sanskrit: yasya̍ mā ha̱rito̱ rathe̍ ti̱sro vaha̍nti sādhu̱yā | stavai̍ sa̱hasra̍dakṣiṇe ||
english: Whose three bay horses carry me rightly on his chariot — I would praise him of the thousand sacrificial gifts.

sanskrit: yasya̱ prasvā̍daso̱ gira̍ upa̱maśra̍vasaḥ pi̱tuḥ | kṣetra̱ṁ na ra̱ṇvam ū̱cuṣe̍ ||
english: Whose words are very sweet, of the most famous father, like a joyful field to one who has praised.

sanskrit: adhi̍ putropamaśravo̱ napā̍n mitrātither ihi | pi̱tuṣ ṭe̍ asmi vandi̱tā ||
english: Come here, O Upamaśravas, grandson of Mitrātithi. I am the praiser of your father.

sanskrit: yad īśī̍yā̱mṛtā̍nām u̱ta vā̱ martyā̍nām | jīve̱d in ma̱ghavā̱ mama̍ ||
english: Whether I were lord of immortals or of mortals — may the bounteous one live for me indeed.

sanskrit: na de̱vānā̱m ati̍ vra̱taṁ śa̱tātmā̍ ca̱na jī̍vati | tathā̍ yu̱jā vi vā̍vṛte ||
english: Not even one of a hundred lives beyond the law of the gods; in such wise the yoke-companion has turned away.

sanskrit: prā̱ve̱pā mā̍ bṛha̱to mā̍dayanti pravāte̱jā iri̍ṇe̱ varvṛ̍tānāḥ | soma̍syeva maujava̱tasya̍ bha̱kṣo vi̱bhīda̍ko̱ jāgṛ̍vi̱r mahya̍m acchān ||
english: The big ones born in a gust of wind, rolling in the hollow, exhilarate me as I shake. Like the draught of Soma from mount Mujāvat, the vibhīdaka tree, the wakeful one, has drawn me to itself.

sanskrit: na mā̍ mimetha̱ na ji̍hīḻa e̱ṣā śi̱vā sakhi̍bhya u̱ta mahya̍m āsīt | a̱kṣasyā̱ham e̍kapa̱rasya̍ he̱tor anu̍vratā̱m apa̍ jā̱yām a̍rodham ||
english: She never harmed me, never became angry at me; she was kind to my friends and to me. For the sake of one die, of a single stake, I have driven away my devoted wife.

sanskrit: dveṣṭi̍ śva̱śrūr apa̍ jā̱yā ru̍ṇaddhi̱ na nā̍thi̱to vi̍ndate marḍi̱tāra̍m | aśva̍syeva̱ jara̍to̱ vasnya̍sya̱ nāhaṁ vi̍ndāmi kita̱vasya̱ bhoga̍m ||
english: My mother-in-law hates me; my wife pushes me away; the afflicted one finds no one to take pity on him. Like an old horse put up for sale, I find no use of the gambler.

sanskrit: a̱nye jā̱yām pari̍ mṛśanty asya̱ yasyāgṛ̍dha̱d veda̍ne vā̱jy a1̱̍kṣaḥ | pi̱tā mā̱tā bhrāta̍ra enam āhu̱r na jā̍nīmo̱ naya̍tā ba̱ddham e̱tam ||
english: Others fondle his wife, in the case of him for whose stake the prize die has been greedy. Father, mother, brothers say of him: 'We do not know him; take this bound man away.'

sanskrit: yad ā̱dīdhye̱ na da̍viṣāṇy ebhiḥ parā̱yadbhyo 'va̍ hīye̱ sakhi̍bhyaḥ | nyu̍ptāś ca ba̱bhravo̱ vāca̱m akra̍ta̱m̐ emīd e̍ṣāṁ niṣkṛ̱taṁ jā̱riṇī̍va ||
english: When I resolve that I will not play with them, I am left behind by my departing companions. The brown ones, cast down, have uttered speech — I go to their meeting-place like a strumpet.

sanskrit: sa̱bhām e̍ti kita̱vaḥ pṛ̱cchamā̍no je̱ṣyāmīti̍ ta̱nvā̱3̱̍ śūśu̍jānaḥ | a̱kṣāso̍ asya̱ vi ti̍ranti̱ kāma̍m prati̱dīvne̱ dadha̍ta̱ ā kṛ̱tāni̍ ||
english: The gambler goes to the assembly hall, asking himself 'Will I win?', his body aglow. The dice cross his desire in the opposite direction, giving to his adversary the winnings.

sanskrit: a̱kṣāsa̱ id a̍ṅku̱śino̍ nito̱dino̍ ni̱kṛtvā̍na̱s tapa̍nās tāpayi̱ṣṇava̍ḥ | ku̱mā̱rade̍ṣṇā̱ jaya̍taḥ puna̱rhaṇo̱ madhvā̱ sampṛ̍ktāḥ kita̱vasya̍ ba̱rhaṇā̍ ||
english: The dice indeed are hooked, pricking, deceitful, torturing, scorching. They give gifts like a boy; they strike again and again, smeared with honey, they destroy the gambler.

sanskrit: tri̱pa̱ñcā̱śaḥ krī̍ḻati̱ vrāta̍ eṣāṁ de̱va i̍va savi̱tā sa̱tyadha̍rmā | u̱grasya̍ cin ma̱nyave̱ nā na̍mante̱ rājā̍ cid ebhyo̱ nama̱ it kṛ̍ṇoti ||
english: Their group of fifty-three plays like the god Savitṛ whose laws are true. They bow not even to the wrath of the fierce one; even a king does homage to these dice.

sanskrit: nī̱cā va̍rtanta u̱pari̍ sphuranty aha̱stāso̱ hasta̍vantaṁ sahante | di̱vyā aṅgā̍rā̱ iri̍ṇe̱ nyu̍ptāḥ śī̱tāḥ santo̱ hṛda̍ya̱ṁ nir da̍hanti ||
english: Rolling downward they spring upward; handless, they overpower the one with hands. Heavenly coals cast into the hollow, though cold, they burn the heart through.

sanskrit: jā̱yā ta̍pyate kita̱vasya̍ hī̱nā mā̱tā pu̱trasya̱ cara̍ta̱ḥ kva̍ svit | ṛ̱ṇā̱vā bibhya̱d dhana̍m i̱cchamā̍no̱ 'nyeṣā̱m asta̱m upa̱ nakta̍m eti ||
english: The gambler's abandoned wife burns with grief; the mother grieves for her son wandering — who knows where? In debt, afraid, craving money, he goes at night to the houses of others.

sanskrit: striya̍ṁ dṛ̱ṣṭvāya̍ kita̱vaṁ ta̍tāpā̱nyeṣā̍ṁ jā̱yāṁ sukṛ̍taṁ ca̱ yoni̍m | pū̱rvā̱hṇe aśvā̍n yuyu̱je hi ba̱bhrūn so a̱gner ante̍ vṛṣa̱laḥ pa̍pāda ||
english: It pained him to see the woman — the wives of others and the well-found source — the gambler; he yoked the tawny horses in the morning, and fell as an outcast at the fire's edge.

sanskrit: yo va̍ḥ senā̱nīr ma̍ha̱to ga̱ṇasya̱ rājā̱ vrāta̍sya pratha̱mo ba̱bhūva̍ | tasmai̍ kṛṇomi̱ na dhanā̍ ruṇadhmi̱ daśā̱ham prācī̱s tad ṛ̱taṁ va̍dāmi ||
english: To him who is the general of your great host, who became the first king of the band — to him I render; I do not hold back the wealth. I speak this truth: I offer ten times toward the east.

sanskrit: a̱kṣair mā dī̍vyaḥ kṛ̱ṣim it kṛ̍ṣasva vi̱tte ra̍masva ba̱hu manya̍mānaḥ | tatra̱ gāva̍ḥ kitava̱ tatra̍ jā̱yā tan me̱ vi ca̍ṣṭe savi̱tāyam a̱ryaḥ ||
english: Do not play with dice; till the soil instead; delight in your property, thinking it much. There are the cattle, O gambler, there is your wife — this the noble Savitṛ shows me as the right path.

sanskrit: mi̱traṁ kṛ̍ṇudhva̱ṁ khalu̍ mṛ̱ḻatā̍ no̱ mā no̍ gho̱reṇa̍ caratā̱bhi dhṛ̱ṣṇu | ni vo̱ nu ma̱nyur vi̍śatā̱m arā̍tir a̱nyo ba̍bhrū̱ṇām prasi̍tau̱ nv a̍stu ||
english: Make friendship with us, verily have mercy on us; do not move against us boldly in terrible fashion. Let your wrath subside now, let the enmity enter; let another now be in the thrall of the tawny dice.

sanskrit: abu̍dhram u̱ tya indra̍vanto a̱gnayo̱ jyoti̱r bhara̍nta u̱ṣaso̱ vyu̍ṣṭiṣu | ma̱hī dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī ce̍tatā̱m apo̱ 'dyā de̱vānā̱m ava̱ ā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: Those fires accompanied by Indra awakened, bearing light at the dawning of the Dawns. May great Heaven and Earth be awake, and the Waters — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: di̱vaspṛ̍thi̱vyor ava̱ ā vṛ̍ṇīmahe mā̱tṝn sindhū̱n parva̍tāñ charya̱ṇāva̍taḥ | a̱nā̱gā̱stvaṁ sūrya̍m u̱ṣāsa̍m īmahe bha̱draṁ soma̍ḥ suvā̱no a̱dyā kṛ̍ṇotu naḥ ||
english: We choose the protection of Heaven and Earth; the mothers, the rivers, the mountains of Śaryaṇāvat. We implore the sinlessness of the Sun, of the Dawn; may the pressed Soma make us auspicious today.

sanskrit: dyāvā̍ no a̱dya pṛ̍thi̱vī anā̍gaso ma̱hī trā̍yetāṁ suvi̱tāya̍ mā̱tarā̍ | u̱ṣā u̱cchanty apa̍ bādhatām a̱ghaṁ sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: May Heaven and Earth, the great mothers, protect us today, sinless ones, for our wellbeing. May the Dawn, as she shines out, drive away evil — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: i̱yaṁ na̍ u̱srā pra̍tha̱mā su̍de̱vya̍ṁ re̱vat sa̱nibhyo̍ re̱vatī̱ vy u̍cchatu | ā̱re ma̱nyuṁ du̍rvi̱datra̍sya dhīmahi sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: May this first Dawn of ours, rich in gods, shine forth richly for the winners of wealth, richly. We set the wrath of the evil adversary far away — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: pra yāḥ sisra̍te̱ sūrya̍sya ra̱śmibhi̱r jyoti̱r bhara̍ntīr u̱ṣaso̱ vyu̍ṣṭiṣu | bha̱drā no̍ a̱dya śrava̍se̱ vy u̍cchata sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: She who flows forth with the rays of the Sun, bearing light at the dawning of the Dawns — may she shine today for our glory — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: a̱na̱mī̱vā u̱ṣasa̱ ā ca̍rantu na̱ ud a̱gnayo̍ jihatā̱ṁ jyoti̍ṣā bṛ̱hat | āyu̍kṣātām a̱śvinā̱ tūtu̍ji̱ṁ ratha̍ṁ sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: May disease-free dawns come unto us; may the fires rise high with light. May the Aśvins yoke their swift chariot — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: śreṣṭha̍ṁ no a̱dya sa̍vita̱r vare̍ṇyam bhā̱gam ā su̍va̱ sa hi ra̍tna̱dhā asi̍ | rā̱yo jani̍trīṁ dhi̱ṣaṇā̱m upa̍ bruve sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: O Savitṛ, impel today for us the best, most excellent share, for you are the giver of treasure. I call upon Dhiṣaṇā the mother of riches — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: pipa̍rtu mā̱ tad ṛ̱tasya̍ pra̱vāca̍naṁ de̱vānā̱ṁ yan ma̍nu̱ṣyā̱3̱̍ ama̍nmahi | viśvā̱ id u̱srāḥ spaḻ ud e̍ti̱ sūrya̍ḥ sva̱sty a1̱̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: May that proclamation of Ṛta fill me — what we thought of as belonging to the gods among humans. With all the Dawns the Sun surely rises — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: a̱dve̱ṣo a̱dya ba̱rhiṣa̱ḥ starī̍maṇi̱ grāvṇā̱ṁ yoge̱ manma̍na̱ḥ sādha̍ īmahe | ā̱di̱tyānā̱ṁ śarma̍ṇi̱ sthā bhu̍raṇyasi sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: Without enmity today, upon the strewing of the sacred grass, in the yoking of the pressing stones, we perfect the prayer. You stand firm in the shelter of the Ādityas — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: ā no̍ ba̱rhiḥ sa̍dha̱māde̍ bṛ̱had di̱vi de̱vām̐ ī̍ḻe sā̱dayā̍ sa̱pta hotṝ̍n | indra̍m mi̱traṁ varu̍ṇaṁ sā̱taye̱ bhaga̍ṁ sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: Upon our sacred grass in the great joint-joy of heaven, I invoke the gods — set the seven priests in place. Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Bhaga for conquest — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: ta ā̍dityā̱ ā ga̍tā sa̱rvatā̍taye vṛ̱dhe no̍ ya̱jñam a̍vatā sajoṣasaḥ | bṛha̱spati̍m pū̱ṣaṇa̍m a̱śvinā̱ bhaga̍ṁ sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: Come, O Ādityas, for our complete welfare; protect our sacrifice with one accord, for our growth. Bṛhaspati, Pūṣan, the Aśvins, Bhaga — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: tan no̍ devā yacchata supravāca̱naṁ cha̱rdir ā̍dityāḥ su̱bhara̍ṁ nṛ̱pāyya̍m | paśve̍ to̱kāya̱ tana̍yāya jī̱vase̍ sva̱sty a1̱̍gniṁ sa̍midhā̱nam ī̍mahe ||
english: Grant us, O gods, O Ādityas, this excellent proclamation — shelter well-supported, fit for lords. For cattle, for offspring, for progeny to live — we implore Agni kindled for our welfare.

sanskrit: viśve̍ a̱dya ma̱ruto̱ viśva̍ ū̱tī viśve̍ bhavantv a̱gnaya̱ḥ sami̍ddhāḥ | viśve̍ no de̱vā ava̱sā ga̍mantu̱ viśva̍m astu̱ dravi̍ṇa̱ṁ vājo̍ a̱sme ||
english: All the Maruts today, with all their aids; may all the fires be kindled. May all the gods come to us with protection; may all riches, all vigour be ours.

sanskrit: yaṁ de̍vā̱so 'va̍tha̱ vāja̍sātau̱ yaṁ trāya̍dhve̱ yam pi̍pṛ̱thāty aṁha̍ḥ | yo vo̍ gopī̱the na bha̱yasya̱ veda̱ te syā̍ma de̱vavī̍taye turāsaḥ ||
english: Whom the gods aid in the winning of prizes, whom they protect, whom they fill and save from distress — he who in your herd knows no fear: may we be swift for the feast of the gods.

sanskrit: u̱ṣāsā̱naktā̍ bṛha̱tī su̱peśa̍sā̱ dyāvā̱kṣāmā̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā | indra̍ṁ huve ma̱ruta̱ḥ parva̍tām̐ a̱pa ā̍di̱tyān dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī a̱paḥ sva̍ḥ ||
english: Dawn and Night, the great, well-adorned pair; Heaven and Earth; Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman — I invoke Indra, the Maruts, the mountains, the Waters, the Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and Heaven.

sanskrit: dyauś ca̍ naḥ pṛthi̱vī ca̱ prace̍tasa ṛ̱tāva̍rī rakṣatā̱m aṁha̍so ri̱ṣaḥ | mā du̍rvi̱datrā̱ nirṛ̍tir na īśata̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: May Heaven and Earth, the wise, possessing Ṛta, protect us from distress and harm. May evil-intentioned Nirṛti not rule us — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: viśva̍smān no̱ adi̍tiḥ pā̱tv aṁha̍so mā̱tā mi̱trasya̱ varu̍ṇasya re̱vata̍ḥ | sva̍rva̱j jyoti̍r avṛ̱kaṁ na̍śīmahi̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: May Aditi, mother of the wealthy Mitra and Varuṇa, protect us from all distress. May we attain the light that resembles the sun, free from wolves — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: grāvā̱ vada̱nn apa̱ rakṣā̍ṁsi sedhatu du̱ṣṣvapnya̱ṁ nirṛ̍ti̱ṁ viśva̍m a̱triṇa̍m | ā̱di̱tyaṁ śarma̍ ma̱rutā̍m aśīmahi̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: Let the speaking pressing stone drive away the demons, evil dreams, Nirṛti, all devouring things. May we attain the shelter of the Āditya, of the Maruts — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: endro̍ ba̱rhiḥ sīda̍tu̱ pinva̍tā̱m iḻā̱ bṛha̱spati̱ḥ sāma̍bhir ṛ̱kvo a̍rcatu | su̱pra̱ke̱taṁ jī̱vase̱ manma̍ dhīmahi̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: Let Indra sit upon the sacred grass; let Iḷā swell; let Bṛhaspati praise with hymns and lauds. We set in our heart the thought well-perceived, to live — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: di̱vi̱spṛśa̍ṁ ya̱jñam a̱smāka̍m aśvinā jī̱rādhva̍raṁ kṛṇutaṁ su̱mnam i̱ṣṭaye̍ | prā̱cīna̍raśmi̱m āhu̍taṁ ghṛ̱tena̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: O Aśvins, make our sacrifice sky-touching, swift-coursing, with goodwill for the quest — the oblation with eastward ray, offered with ghee — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: upa̍ hvaye su̱hava̱m māru̍taṁ ga̱ṇam pā̍va̱kam ṛ̱ṣvaṁ sa̱khyāya̍ śa̱mbhuva̍m | rā̱yas poṣa̍ṁ sauśrava̱sāya̍ dhīmahi̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: I call upon the Marutas host, easy to call, purifying, noble, beneficent, for friendship. We set in our heart the swelling of riches, for good fame — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: a̱pām peru̍ṁ jī̱vadha̍nyam bharāmahe devā̱vya̍ṁ su̱hava̍m adhvara̱śriya̍m | su̱ra̱śmiṁ soma̍m indri̱yaṁ ya̍mīmahi̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: We bring the invigorating Soma of the waters, fit for the gods, easy to invoke, the glory of the sacrifice. We control the bright-rayed, Indra-meant Soma — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: sa̱nema̱ tat su̍sa̱nitā̍ sa̱nitva̍bhir va̱yaṁ jī̱vā jī̱vapu̍trā̱ anā̍gasaḥ | bra̱hma̱dviṣo̱ viṣva̱g eno̍ bharerata̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: May we win that through excellent winning with our winnings — we, living, with living sons, sinless. Let those who hate sacred knowledge bear their sin in every direction — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: ye sthā mano̍r ya̱jñiyā̱s te śṛ̍ṇotana̱ yad vo̍ devā̱ īma̍he̱ tad da̍dātana | jaitra̱ṁ kratu̍ṁ rayi̱mad vī̱rava̱d yaśa̱s tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: You who are among Manu's gods of sacrifice, listen — what we implore of you, O gods, give that. A victorious resolve, riches, heroic fame — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: ma̱had a̱dya ma̍ha̱tām ā vṛ̍ṇīma̱he 'vo̍ de̱vānā̍ṁ bṛha̱tām a̍na̱rvaṇā̍m | yathā̱ vasu̍ vī̱rajā̍ta̱ṁ naśā̍mahai̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: Today we choose the great protection of the great gods, of the vast unchallenged ones. So that we may reach wealth born of vigour — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: ma̱ho a̱gneḥ sa̍midhā̱nasya̱ śarma̱ṇy anā̍gā mi̱tre varu̍ṇe sva̱staye̍ | śreṣṭhe̍ syāma savi̱tuḥ savī̍mani̱ tad de̱vānā̱m avo̍ a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: In the great shelter of Agni blazing, sinless in Mitra and Varuṇa for welfare — may we be in the best impulsion of Savitṛ — today we choose the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: ye sa̍vi̱tuḥ sa̱tyasa̍vasya̱ viśve̍ mi̱trasya̍ vra̱te varu̍ṇasya de̱vāḥ | te saubha̍gaṁ vī̱rava̱d goma̱d apno̱ dadhā̍tana̱ dravi̍ṇaṁ ci̱tram a̱sme ||
english: All the gods who are in the vow of Savitṛ of true might, in the vow of Mitra, of Varuṇa — may they bestow on us auspiciousness with heroes, with cattle, with substance and brilliant wealth.

sanskrit: sa̱vi̱tā pa̱ścātā̍t savi̱tā pu̱rastā̍t savi̱totta̱rāttā̍t savi̱tādha̱rāttā̍t | sa̱vi̱tā na̍ḥ suvatu sa̱rvatā̍tiṁ savi̱tā no̍ rāsatāṁ dī̱rgham āyu̍ḥ ||
english: Savitṛ from the west, Savitṛ from the east, Savitṛ from the north, Savitṛ from below — may Savitṛ impel us toward complete welfare; may Savitṛ grant us long life.

sanskrit: namo̍ mi̱trasya̱ varu̍ṇasya̱ cakṣa̍se ma̱ho de̱vāya̱ tad ṛ̱taṁ sa̍paryata | dū̱re̱dṛśe̍ de̱vajā̍tāya ke̱tave̍ di̱vas pu̱trāya̱ sūryā̍ya śaṁsata ||
english: Reverence to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, to the great god — attend to that Ṛta. Proclaim the far-seeing, divine-born banner, the son of Heaven, the Sun.

sanskrit: sā mā̍ sa̱tyokti̱ḥ pari̍ pātu vi̱śvato̱ dyāvā̍ ca̱ yatra̍ ta̱tana̱nn ahā̍ni ca | viśva̍m a̱nyan ni vi̍śate̱ yad eja̍ti vi̱śvāhāpo̍ vi̱śvāhod e̍ti̱ sūrya̍ḥ ||
english: May that truthful utterance guard me on all sides, there where the days are stretched out and the Heavens. Everything else that moves enters into rest; the Sun goes forth every day, every day.

sanskrit: na te̱ ade̍vaḥ pra̱divo̱ ni vā̍sate̱ yad e̍ta̱śebhi̍ḥ pata̱rai ra̍tha̱ryasi̍ | prā̱cīna̍m a̱nyad anu̍ vartate̱ raja̱ ud a̱nyena̱ jyoti̍ṣā yāsi sūrya ||
english: No godless one abides before you from days of old, when you career with winged steeds. One realm follows in the east; you go upward, O Sūrya, with another light.

sanskrit: yena̍ sūrya̱ jyoti̍ṣā̱ bādha̍se̱ tamo̱ jaga̍c ca̱ viśva̍m udi̱yarṣi̍ bhā̱nunā̍ | tenā̱smad viśvā̱m ani̍rā̱m anā̍huti̱m apāmī̍vā̱m apa̍ du̱ṣṣvapnya̍ṁ suva ||
english: With that light with which you thrust away darkness, O Sūrya, and raise up the whole world with your beam — with that, drive away from us all weakness, all that is unfit for offering, all disease, all evil dreams.

sanskrit: viśva̍sya̱ hi preṣi̍to̱ rakṣa̍si vra̱tam ahe̍ḻayann u̱ccara̍si sva̱dhā anu̍ | yad a̱dya tvā̍ sūryopa̱bravā̍mahai̱ taṁ no̍ de̱vā anu̍ maṁsīrata̱ kratu̍m ||
english: Sent by all, you guard the law without anger; you rise by your own power. Whatever resolve we make today calling upon you, O Sūrya, may the gods approve that resolve of ours.

sanskrit: taṁ no̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī tan na̱ āpa̱ indra̍ḥ śṛṇvantu ma̱ruto̱ hava̱ṁ vaca̍ḥ | mā śūne̍ bhūma̱ sūrya̍sya sa̱ṁdṛśi̍ bha̱draṁ jīva̍nto jara̱ṇām a̍śīmahi ||
english: May Heaven and Earth, the Waters, Indra, the Maruts hear this call of our voice. May we not be empty in the sight of Sūrya; living, may we attain an auspicious old age.

sanskrit: vi̱śvāhā̍ tvā su̱mana̍saḥ su̱cakṣa̍saḥ pra̱jāva̍nto anamī̱vā anā̍gasaḥ | u̱dyanta̍ṁ tvā mitramaho di̱ve-di̍ve̱ jyog jī̱vāḥ prati̍ paśyema sūrya ||
english: Always, of glad heart, with good sight, with progeny, free from disease, sinless — may we see you rising, O Sūrya of friendly greatness, day by day, living long.

sanskrit: mahi̱ jyoti̱r bibhra̍taṁ tvā vicakṣaṇa̱ bhāsva̍nta̱ṁ cakṣu̍ṣe-cakṣuṣe̱ maya̍ḥ | ā̱roha̍ntam bṛha̱taḥ pāja̍sa̱s pari̍ va̱yaṁ jī̱vāḥ prati̍ paśyema sūrya ||
english: You who bear the great light, the discerning one, the radiant delight of every eye — as you mount around the great expanse, may we see you, O Sūrya, living.

sanskrit: yasya̍ te̱ viśvā̱ bhuva̍nāni ke̱tunā̱ pra cera̍te̱ ni ca̍ vi̱śante̍ a̱ktubhi̍ḥ | a̱nā̱gā̱stvena̍ harikeśa sū̱ryāhnā̍hnā no̱ vasya̍sā-vasya̱sod i̍hi ||
english: By whose banner all beings go forth, and by whose nights they enter into rest — with sinlessness, O golden-haired Sūrya, day by day rise for us more and more enriching.

sanskrit: śaṁ no̍ bhava̱ cakṣa̍sā̱ śaṁ no̱ ahnā̱ śam bhā̱nunā̱ śaṁ hi̱mā śaṁ ghṛ̱ṇena̍ | yathā̱ śam adhva̱ñ cham asa̍d duro̱ṇe tat sū̍rya̱ dravi̍ṇaṁ dhehi ci̱tram ||
english: Be auspicious to us with your light, auspicious to us with the day, auspicious with your beam, auspicious with your cold, auspicious with your warmth. As it may be auspicious on the way and auspicious in the house — O Sūrya, grant us brilliant wealth.

sanskrit: a̱smāka̍ṁ devā u̱bhayā̍ya̱ janma̍ne̱ śarma̍ yacchata dvi̱pade̱ catu̍ṣpade | a̱dat piba̍d ū̱rjaya̍māna̱m āśi̱taṁ tad a̱sme śaṁ yor a̍ra̱po da̍dhātana ||
english: O gods, extend shelter to both our births — to the two-footed and to the four-footed. May he eat, drink, be invigorated, be satisfied — place that healing and welfare free from harm in us.

sanskrit: yad vo̍ devāś cakṛ̱ma ji̱hvayā̍ gu̱ru mana̍so vā̱ prayu̍tī deva̱heḻa̍nam | arā̍vā̱ yo no̍ a̱bhi du̍cchunā̱yate̱ tasmi̱n tad eno̍ vasavo̱ ni dhe̍tana ||
english: Whatever offense toward the gods we have made with the tongue, or through the impulse of mind, O Vasus — the hostile one who wishes ill upon us, place that sin upon him.

sanskrit: a̱smin na̍ indra pṛtsu̱tau yaśa̍svati̱ śimī̍vati̱ kranda̍si̱ prāva̍ sā̱taye̍ | yatra̱ goṣā̍tā dhṛṣi̱teṣu̍ khā̱diṣu̱ viṣva̱k pata̍nti di̱dyavo̍ nṛ̱ṣāhye̍ ||
english: In this glorious, energetic battle-shout, help us, O Indra, for conquest — where the cattle-winning missiles fly in all directions against the brave men, in the bold raids.

sanskrit: sa na̍ḥ kṣu̱manta̱ṁ sada̍ne̱ vy ū̍rṇuhi̱ goa̍rṇasaṁ ra̱yim i̍ndra śra̱vāyya̍m | syāma̍ te̱ jaya̍taḥ śakra me̱dino̱ yathā̍ va̱yam u̱śmasi̱ tad va̍so kṛdhi ||
english: Uncover for us in the dwelling a wealth full of grain, of cattle, worthy of fame, O Indra. May we be the allies of you who are victorious, O Mighty One — O Vasu, do as we desire.

sanskrit: yo no̱ dāsa̱ āryo̍ vā puruṣṭu̱tāde̍va indra yu̱dhaye̱ cike̍tati | a̱smābhi̍ṣ ṭe su̱ṣahā̍ḥ santu̱ śatra̍va̱s tvayā̍ va̱yaṁ tān va̍nuyāma saṁga̱me ||
english: Whether the Dāsa or the Ārya who, O much-praised Indra, plans to fight against us the godless — may your enemies be easy to overcome with us; may we, with you, win them in battle.

sanskrit: yo da̱bhrebhi̱r havyo̱ yaś ca̱ bhūri̍bhi̱r yo a̱bhīke̍ varivo̱vin nṛ̱ṣāhye̍ | taṁ vi̍khā̱de sasni̍m a̱dya śru̱taṁ nara̍m a̱rvāñca̱m indra̱m ava̍se karāmahe ||
english: He who is to be invoked with few gifts and he who is with many, who clears a wide path in the man-conquering fray — we turn today toward that famous winning hero, we turn Indra toward us for aid.

sanskrit: sva̱vṛja̱ṁ hi tvām a̱ham i̍ndra śu̱śravā̍nānu̱daṁ vṛ̍ṣabha radhra̱coda̍nam | pra mu̍ñcasva̱ pari̱ kutsā̍d i̱hā ga̍hi̱ kim u̱ tvāvā̍n mu̱ṣkayo̍r ba̱ddha ā̍sate ||
english: For I have heard you, O Indra, as self-choosing, unstoppable, O bull, spurring on the weak. Free yourself from Kutsa; come here — why would one like you remain bound by the testicles?

sanskrit: yo vā̱m pari̍jmā su̱vṛd a̍śvinā̱ ratho̍ do̱ṣām u̱ṣāso̱ havyo̍ ha̱viṣma̍tā | śa̱śva̱tta̱māsa̱s tam u̍ vām i̱daṁ va̱yam pi̱tur na nāma̍ su̱hava̍ṁ havāmahe ||
english: That circuit-running, well-turning chariot of yours, O Aśvins, called upon with oblation from evening to dawn, most frequent — this of yours we also invoke by the easy-to-call name as a son calls his father.

sanskrit: co̱daya̍taṁ sū̱nṛtā̱ḥ pinva̍ta̱ṁ dhiya̱ ut pura̍ṁdhīr īrayata̱ṁ tad u̍śmasi | ya̱śasa̍m bhā̱gaṁ kṛ̍ṇutaṁ no aśvinā̱ soma̱ṁ na cāru̍m ma̱ghava̍tsu nas kṛtam ||
english: Set in motion kindly truths; swell up our prayers; stir up full minds — this we desire. Make our portion glorious, O Aśvins, and grant us lovely Soma among the bounteous.

sanskrit: a̱mā̱jura̍ś cid bhavatho yu̱vam bhago̍ 'nā̱śoś ci̍d avi̱tārā̍pa̱masya̍ cit | a̱ndhasya̍ cin nāsatyā kṛ̱śasya̍ cid yu̱vām id ā̍hur bhi̱ṣajā̍ ru̱tasya̍ cit ||
english: Though the lot be ageing in the house, you two become its helpers; of one who is decaying, of one who is nearly lost. Even of the blind, O Nāsatyas, and of the emaciated — you two are called the healers even of the broken.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ cyavā̍naṁ sa̱naya̱ṁ yathā̱ ratha̱m puna̱r yuvā̍naṁ ca̱rathā̍ya takṣathuḥ | niṣ ṭau̱gryam ū̍hathur a̱dbhyas pari̱ viśvet tā vā̱ṁ sava̍neṣu pra̱vācyā̍ ||
english: You fashioned Cyavana, old as an ancient chariot, into a young man again for movement. You carried Tugra's son across from the waters — all these deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the pressings.

sanskrit: pu̱rā̱ṇā vā̍ṁ vī̱ryā̱3̱̍ pra bra̍vā̱ jane 'tho̍ hāsathur bhi̱ṣajā̍ mayo̱bhuvā̍ | tā vā̱ṁ nu navyā̱v ava̍se karāmahe̱ 'yaṁ nā̍satyā̱ śrad a̱rir yathā̱ dadha̍t ||
english: I will declare your ancient heroic deeds to the people; you have also been healers, producers of bliss. We now invoke these two of yours, fresh, for our protection — may this worshipper place faith in you, O Nāsatyas, as a friend.

sanskrit: i̱yaṁ vā̍m ahve śṛṇu̱tam me̍ aśvinā pu̱trāye̍va pi̱tarā̱ mahya̍ṁ śikṣatam | anā̍pi̱r ajñā̍ asajā̱tyāma̍tiḥ pu̱rā tasyā̍ a̱bhiśa̍ste̱r ava̍ spṛtam ||
english: This is my call to you — hear me, O Aśvins; teach me like parents teach a son. Friendless, ignorant, unfitted of birth, of wrong understanding — before that reproach, rescue me.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ rathe̍na vima̱dāya̍ śu̱ndhyuva̱ṁ ny ū̍hathuḥ purumi̱trasya̱ yoṣa̍ṇām | yu̱vaṁ hava̍ṁ vadhrima̱tyā a̍gacchataṁ yu̱vaṁ suṣu̍tiṁ cakrathu̱ḥ pura̍ṁdhaye ||
english: You two brought the bride of Purumitra to Vimada in your chariot, the lovely one. You two heeded the call of Vadhrīmatī; you two granted good birth to Puraṁdhī.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ vipra̍sya jara̱ṇām u̍pe̱yuṣa̱ḥ puna̍ḥ ka̱ler a̍kṛṇuta̱ṁ yuva̱d vaya̍ḥ | yu̱vaṁ vanda̍nam ṛśya̱dād ud ū̍pathur yu̱vaṁ sa̱dyo vi̱śpalā̱m eta̍ve kṛthaḥ ||
english: For the inspired one who had come to old age, you two made youthful vigour again. You two raised Vandana up from the Ṛśyad; you two straightway made Viśpalā able to go.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ ha̍ re̱bhaṁ vṛ̍ṣaṇā̱ guhā̍ hi̱tam ud ai̍rayatam mamṛ̱vāṁsa̍m aśvinā | yu̱vam ṛ̱bīsa̍m u̱ta ta̱ptam atra̍ya̱ oma̍nvantaṁ cakrathuḥ sa̱ptava̍dhraye ||
english: You two, O mighty Aśvins, raised up Rebha who lay hidden, as if dead. You two made Atri, enclosed in the pit and scorched, find comfort — for Saptavadhri you two did the same.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ śve̱tam pe̱dave̍ 'śvi̱nāśva̍ṁ na̱vabhi̱r vājai̍r nava̱tī ca̍ vā̱jina̍m | ca̱rkṛtya̍ṁ dadathur drāva̱yatsa̍kha̱m bhaga̱ṁ na nṛbhyo̱ havya̍m mayo̱bhuva̍m ||
english: You two gave to Pedu, O Aśvins, a white horse with nine times nine prizes — ever-active, companion-scattering — like Bhaga, a prize invoked by men, a producer of bliss.

sanskrit: na taṁ rā̍jānāv adite̱ kuta̍ś ca̱na nāṁho̍ aśnoti duri̱taṁ naki̍r bha̱yam | yam a̍śvinā suhavā rudravartanī purora̱thaṁ kṛ̍ṇu̱thaḥ patnyā̍ sa̱ha ||
english: Not from anywhere does distress reach him, O Aditi, nor does evil or any fear — the one whom you Aśvins, easy to call, of fierce course, make to go before the chariot together with his wife.

sanskrit: ā tena̍ yāta̱m mana̍so̱ javī̍yasā̱ ratha̱ṁ yaṁ vā̍m ṛ̱bhava̍ś ca̱krur a̍śvinā | yasya̱ yoge̍ duhi̱tā jāya̍te di̱va u̱bhe aha̍nī su̱dine̍ vi̱vasva̍taḥ ||
english: Come with that chariot, swifter than thought, which the Ṛbhus fashioned for you, O Aśvins — at whose yoking the daughter of Heaven is born, both days of Vivasvat being auspicious.

sanskrit: tā va̱rtir yā̍taṁ ja̱yuṣā̱ vi parva̍ta̱m api̍nvataṁ śa̱yave̍ dhe̱num a̍śvinā | vṛka̍sya ci̱d varti̍kām a̱ntar ā̱syā̍d yu̱vaṁ śacī̍bhir grasi̱tām a̍muñcatam ||
english: Come along that path, victorious over the mountain; you swelled the milk-cow for Śayu, O Aśvins. Even the quail from the jaw of the wolf — you two with your powers released her who had been swallowed.

sanskrit: e̱taṁ vā̱ṁ stoma̍m aśvināv aka̱rmāta̍kṣāma̱ bhṛga̍vo̱ na ratha̍m | ny a̍mṛkṣāma̱ yoṣa̍ṇā̱ṁ na marye̱ nitya̱ṁ na sū̱nuṁ tana̍ya̱ṁ dadhā̍nāḥ ||
english: This praise for you, O Aśvins, we have made; we have fashioned it as the Bhṛgus fashion a chariot. We have polished it as a young man polishes his bride, holding it constantly as a son and child.

sanskrit: ratha̱ṁ yānta̱ṁ kuha̱ ko ha̍ vāṁ narā̱ prati̍ dyu̱manta̍ṁ suvi̱tāya̍ bhūṣati | prā̱ta̱ryāvā̍ṇaṁ vi̱bhva̍ṁ vi̱śe-vi̍śe̱ vasto̍r-vasto̱r vaha̍mānaṁ dhi̱yā śami̍ ||
english: Where, O heroes, who adorns your bright chariot as it comes for your blessing? I prepare with thought the early-travelling, far-reaching one, carried from dwelling to dwelling, folk to folk.

sanskrit: kuha̍ svid do̱ṣā kuha̱ vasto̍r a̱śvinā̱ kuhā̍bhipi̱tvaṁ ka̍rata̱ḥ kuho̍ṣatuḥ | ko vā̍ṁ śayu̱trā vi̱dhave̍va de̱vara̱m marya̱ṁ na yoṣā̍ kṛṇute sa̱dhastha̱ ā ||
english: Where were you at evening, O Aśvins, where at dawn? Where do you make your approach? Where do you dwell? Who invites you to rest, as a widow invites a brother-in-law, as a young woman invites a young man to her seat?

sanskrit: prā̱tar ja̍rethe jara̱ṇeva̱ kāpa̍yā̱ vasto̍r-vastor yaja̱tā ga̍cchatho gṛ̱ham | kasya̍ dhva̱srā bha̍vatha̱ḥ kasya̍ vā narā rājapu̱treva̱ sava̱nāva̍ gacchathaḥ ||
english: In the morning you delight like an old woman of the Kāpī clan; from dwelling to dwelling, O adorable ones, you go to the house. Whose wonderworkers do you become, O heroes, or as king's sons do you go to whose pressings?

sanskrit: yu̱vām mṛ̱geva̍ vāra̱ṇā mṛ̍ga̱ṇyavo̍ do̱ṣā vasto̍r ha̱viṣā̱ ni hva̍yāmahe | yu̱vaṁ hotrā̍m ṛtu̱thā juhva̍te na̱reṣa̱ṁ janā̍ya vahathaḥ śubhas patī ||
english: Like two wild bulls, hunted by hunters, we call upon you two at evening and dawn with oblation. You bring the priestly office, performed in season, to those men who offer — to the people, O lords of beauty.

sanskrit: yu̱vāṁ ha̱ ghoṣā̱ pary a̍śvinā ya̱tī rājña̍ ūce duhi̱tā pṛ̱cche vā̍ṁ narā | bhū̱tam me̱ ahna̍ u̱ta bhū̍tam a̱ktave 'śvā̍vate ra̱thine̍ śakta̱m arva̍te ||
english: Ghoṣā seeking you, O Aśvins, the king's daughter, said — I ask you, O heroes: be present for me by day, and be present at night; grant me the ability to win a husband with horses and a chariot.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ ka̱vī ṣṭha̱ḥ pary a̍śvinā̱ ratha̱ṁ viśo̱ na kutso̍ jari̱tur na̍śāyathaḥ | yu̱vor ha̱ makṣā̱ pary a̍śvinā̱ madhv ā̱sā bha̍rata niṣkṛ̱taṁ na yoṣa̍ṇā ||
english: You two are the seers, O Aśvins, concerning the chariot; like Kutsa the singer you two seek the folk. Swiftly at your mouths, O Aśvins, bear honey, like an adorned maiden.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ ha̍ bhu̱jyuṁ yu̱vam a̍śvinā̱ vaśa̍ṁ yu̱vaṁ śi̱ñjāra̍m u̱śanā̱m upā̍rathuḥ | yu̱vo rarā̍vā̱ pari̍ sa̱khyam ā̍sate yu̱vor a̱ham ava̍sā su̱mnam ā ca̍ke ||
english: You two rescued Bhujyu, O Aśvins, you two rescued Vaśa, you two came to Śiñjāra through Uśanā. The bounteous ones sit around your companionship; I long for your goodwill, your protection.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ ha̍ kṛ̱śaṁ yu̱vam a̍śvinā śa̱yuṁ yu̱vaṁ vi̱dhanta̍ṁ vi̱dhavā̍m uruṣyathaḥ | yu̱vaṁ sa̱nibhya̍ḥ sta̱naya̍ntam aśvi̱nāpa̍ vra̱jam ū̍rṇuthaḥ sa̱ptāsya̍m ||
english: You two rescue the emaciated, O Aśvins, you two the lying sick, you two the worshipper and the widow. From the winning prizes you open for the Aśvins the thundering fold of seven mouths.

sanskrit: jani̍ṣṭa̱ yoṣā̍ pa̱taya̍t kanīna̱ko vi cāru̍han vī̱rudho̍ da̱ṁsanā̱ anu̍ | āsmai̍ rīyante niva̱neva̱ sindha̍vo̱ 'smā ahne̍ bhavati̱ tat pa̍titva̱nam ||
english: The maiden was born; the boy flies away; he strikes the plants beautifully along their magic power. For him the rivers flow as into a hollow; for this day his flight comes into being.

sanskrit: jī̱vaṁ ru̍danti̱ vi ma̍yante adhva̱re dī̱rghām anu̱ prasi̍tiṁ dīdhiyu̱r nara̍ḥ | vā̱mam pi̱tṛbhyo̱ ya i̱daṁ sa̍meri̱re maya̱ḥ pati̍bhyo̱ jana̍yaḥ pari̱ṣvaje̍ ||
english: Weeping for the living one, they part at the sacrifice; the men have contemplated the long continuation. Those who have assembled this loveliness for the fathers, the women embrace bliss for their husbands.

sanskrit: na tasya̍ vidma̱ tad u̱ ṣu pra vo̍cata̱ yuvā̍ ha̱ yad yu̍va̱tyāḥ kṣeti̱ yoni̍ṣu | pri̱yosri̍yasya vṛṣa̱bhasya̍ re̱tino̍ gṛ̱haṁ ga̍memāśvinā̱ tad u̍śmasi ||
english: We do not know that — tell us indeed — when the young man dwells in the womb of the young woman. We desire, O Aśvins, to go to the house of that beloved potent bull, the seed-sower.

sanskrit: ā vā̍m agan suma̱tir vā̍jinīvasū̱ ny a̍śvinā hṛ̱tsu kāmā̍ ayaṁsata | abhū̍taṁ go̱pā mi̍thu̱nā śu̍bhas patī pri̱yā a̍rya̱mṇo duryā̍m̐ aśīmahi ||
english: May your benevolence come, O Aśvins rich in prizes; desires have settled in our hearts. Become guardians as a pair, O lords of beauty — may we attain the dear houses of Aryaman.

sanskrit: tā ma̍ndasā̱nā manu̍ṣo duro̱ṇa ā dha̱ttaṁ ra̱yiṁ sa̱havī̍raṁ vaca̱syave̍ | kṛ̱taṁ tī̱rthaṁ su̍prapā̱ṇaṁ śu̍bhas patī sthā̱ṇum pa̍the̱ṣṭhām apa̍ durma̱tiṁ ha̍tam ||
english: You two, gladdened in the house of Manu, place wealth together with heroes for him who would praise. The ford is made, the good drinking place, O lords of beauty; strike down the evil mind that stands on the path.

sanskrit: kva̍ svid a̱dya ka̍ta̱māsv a̱śvinā̍ vi̱kṣu da̱srā mā̍dayete śu̱bhas patī̍ | ka ī̱ṁ ni ye̍me kata̱masya̍ jagmatu̱r vipra̍sya vā̱ yaja̍mānaṁ vā gṛ̱ham ||
english: Where today, O wonderful Aśvins, lords of beauty, among which peoples do you two delight? Who has guided them? To whose house have they gone — the inspired singer's or the sacrificer's?
